audit.whatIsWrong: Five rows contradicted both the packet and the prose beneath them. The page read Skill / Riven / Riven / Skill / Skill / Riven / Riven while whys[1] says the lane swings 'to him', whys[2] says 'you lose extended trades decisively', whys[3] says 'you cannot burst him faster than his passive absorbs it', and whys[5] says extended fights are 'losing for you'.
audit.why: Twisted Advance is a targeted, untargetable dash-root at 525 range on 14s — from Level 2 onward Maokai can start any trade he wants and Riven cannot refuse it. Handing her Levels 2 and 3 on the chart while the text explains why she loses them is the two-answers-to-one-question failure. Row 4 (Level 6, Skill) and row 6 (2+ items, Riven) already agreed and are left alone; row 6 deliberately follows the mirror rather than the packet, because both layers already say Riven and whys[6] and late argue it.
audit.corrected: Proposed as one atomic chart group in matched full/content pairs: row 0 -> Riven, rows 1, 2, 3 and 5 -> Maokai, with ratings 7/10, 3/10, 3/10, 3/10, 3/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page names Maokai's ultimate 'Vengeful Maelstrom' in whys[4], spikes[2].text and mid, and describes it as an ability that 'reduces incoming poke' and 'denies poke'. That is a reworked-away version of the champion. His ultimate is Nature's Grasp: a wall of brambles that advances forward, damaging and rooting anything in its path, 3000 range on 130/110/90s. It is an engage and a zoning tool, not damage mitigation. Separately, mid gives Twisted Advance an '11-second base CD' and whys[3] says his chain repeats 'every 11 seconds'; it is 14/13/12/11/10.
audit.why: These two errors point the player in opposite directions from the truth. She is told his ultimate makes him harder to poke, so she disengages when she should be watching for a root wall rolling at her from off-screen — a wall that will catch her mid-dash and hand him the fight. And an 11-second W means she steps up three seconds before it is actually down at rank 1, which is precisely the window the root exists to punish.
audit.corrected: Nature's Grasp named with its rooting-wall behaviour, 3000 range and 130s cooldown in whys[4], spikes[2].text and mid. Twisted Advance's real 14-to-10s written into whys[3], mid, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t, alongside Bramble Smash's 7s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing tells the player Twisted Advance makes him untargetable.
audit.why: missingInteractions flags untargetable-dodges-burst. Riot's text is explicit: he 'contorts into a mass of moving roots, becoming untargetable and dashing to the target'. For a champion whose whole pattern is a committed burst rotation, this is the difference between a wasted combo and a won trade — every point of damage aimed at him while the dash is in flight is thrown away, and the correct response is to hold the burst until he lands.
audit.corrected: wants.you[1] rewritten to hold burst through the dash rather than 'punish the whiff', and the untargetable window stated in dosFull[0].d and report[5].t.

audit.why: report[8].t already carries 'Executioner's Calling early — his healing fights your pattern', and unlike several other pages in this slice, here it is true: Sap Magic heals him on attack and its cooldown drops every time he casts a spell or is hit by one. missingInteractions confirms needs-antiheal.
audit.corrected: No change to the item line. The cooldown-refund mechanic added to mid so the player understands why the heal comes back faster in a long trade than in a short one.

edits.before: Level 6 is the only real window you have to force a result before his tank scaling takes over. Pop R and look for Wind Slash execute if you have landed an early lead — his pool of HP is wide but his mobility is near-zero, so a full Q-W-Q-E-Q-Wind Slash rotation does lethal damage if he is below 60% HP. The catch: his W root into saplings into R Vengeful Maelstrom is a slow kill if he plays it defensively, and his passive sustain means drawn-out skirmishes fill him back up between spell casts. Do not burn your combo into a healthy Maokai expecting a quick kill — wait for his W to be on cooldown (11-second base CD), then E-dash to dodge the next cast and all-in him while he is gapless. If you cannot force a clean kill by the time his first tank item arrives, shove and roam rather than continuing a trade that increasingly favours him.
edits.after: Level 6 is the only real window you have to force a result before his tank scaling takes over. Pop R and look for Wind Slash execute if you have landed an early lead — his pool of HP is wide but his mobility is near-zero, so a full Q-W-Q-E-Q-Wind Slash rotation does lethal damage if he is below 60% HP. Do not burn your combo into a healthy Maokai expecting a quick kill — wait for Twisted Advance to be on cooldown (14s at rank 1), then E-dash the next cast and all-in him while he is gapless. unverified: The kit file puts a grounding flag on Bramble Smash (Q). Riot's text describes only a knockback, damage and a slow. Against a three-dash champion, grounding would be decisive, so it should not be asserted from a flag that the description does not support. Nothing I wrote depends on it.

The claim in early that Twisted Advance has 'no travel time to dodge once he commits'. Riot's text says he dashes to the target, which implies travel time; but whether Riven can break the lock with a dash is not in the kit file either way, so I left the sentence alone rather than swap one unverified claim for another.
